column3: NKJV includes “and wanted to judge him according to our law,” following the Textus Receptus; the critical text ends the verse at “we seized him.”
This verse is absent from the critical text; NKJV includes it following the Textus Receptus (Lysias took him by force).
NKJV includes “commanding his accusers to come to you,” following the Textus Receptus; the critical text lacks it, so “him” refers to Paul rather than Lysias.
NKJV includes “of the dead,” following the Textus Receptus; the critical text lacks it.
Close to the Greek; NKJV moves “some Jews from Asia,” which opens verse 19 in Greek, to the end of verse 18.
Close to the Greek; its opening words “some Jews from Asia” appear at the end of verse 18 in NKJV.
NKJV includes “when Felix heard these things,” following the Textus Receptus; the critical text lacks it.
NKJV includes “or visit,” following the Textus Receptus; the critical text lacks it.
NKJV has “faith in Christ,” following the Textus Receptus; the critical text reads “faith in Christ Jesus.”
NKJV includes “that he might release him,” following the Textus Receptus; the critical text lacks it.
